quote: All four now pass our checks.
problem: Round 10 withdrew round 9's "all four versions pass" because the rotation check failed one run in three, and the same paragraph then blocks release 5.0.8 on that very check.
fix: Write: "All four passed the fixture and restart checks. A later review found the rotation check itself was flaky, and release 5.0.8 loses every byte appended after rotation, in five of five runs, so it is blocked."

quote: Two external reviews retracted every collector regex cost figure.
problem: One external review, round 9, retracted them as wall-clock measurements.
fix: Write: "An external review retracted every collector regex cost figure."

quote: At 82~\% of the cap the collector absorbs the shortfall and loses nothing.
problem: The sentence follows a paragraph about the 42,000 a second ceiling, so "the cap" reads as a rate, while it is the 256 MB disk buffer from four paragraphs earlier.
source: reports/loggy-report/briefs/soak-2.md:41 — "backlog 210.7 MB (82 % of cap), 0 dropped ... the 256 MB storage.total_limit_size cap"; soak-2.md:42 gives the 1.8 % and the 262.8 s drain at the same cap.
fix: "At 82~\% of the 256~MB buffer cap the collector absorbs the shortfall and loses nothing."

quote: The re-run rig, the same laptop slowed, offered 5,000.
source: reports/loggy-report/briefs/soak-index.md:17 — "A 47-cell re-run on 27 August at 5,000 a second".

quote: In Round 1, at up to 53,000 records a second, the collector's memory sat between 133 and 228~MB.
problem: The subsection that carries the collector's cost opens on internal round numbering instead of the result.
fix: "The collector's memory sat between 133 and 228~MB at every rate up to 53,000 records a second."

quote: The collector had never read three of the six sources. Six, because the process tree has two line formats.
problem: The report counts five families in 2.1 and 3.1 and six sources here, and then names "the data-distribution format", which 2.1 never named as one of the two process-tree formats.
fix: Name the two formats in Table 1 and 2.1, then write: "The collector had never read three of the five families: the data-distribution format of the process tree, the InfoLogger daemon log and the system journal."

quote: Fixed, severity comes out of 99.83~\% of process-tree lines against a 99~\% gate.
problem: The opening participle has no actor, and round 1 flagged this exact construction, which was removed from 3.4 and left here.
fix: "We fixed the anchor. Severity now comes out of 99.83~\% of process-tree lines, against a 99~\% gate."

quote: At a median worker's 23 records a second, that share is 13.8, and the buffer covers 17.4~hours.
problem: 13.8 carries no unit, so the reader has to derive that it means InfoLogger records a second, and 46.8 repeats the pattern in the next sentence.
fix: "At a median worker's 23 records a second, InfoLogger is 13.8 records a second, and the buffer covers 17.4~hours. At the busiest worker-second, 78, InfoLogger is 46.8 a second and the buffer covers 5.1~hours."

quote: A produce and a consume step raise the live lane's 1-second latency floor.
problem: The same argument counts against the Kafka bus Section 4 agrees for exactly that lane, and the report never says why the cost is acceptable there.
source: briefs/soak-2.md:59 (the 1-second floor, "a produce and a consume step would add to it"); briefs/why.md:120-123 (the live-lane bus is agreed for decoupling, not durability)
fix: Either drop the sentence from Section 5.3, whose other two cost points stand alone, or add one clause in Section 4: "The bus adds a produce and a consume step to that 1-second floor, and the review accepted it for the decoupling."

quote: Later rounds added the data-distribution format, the InfoLogger daemon log and the system journal.
problem: The reader read the data-distribution format as DDS, which Section 2.1 already lists as a collected family; it is in fact the second line format of the O2 process tree.
source: briefs/constraints.md:107-110 (the two O2 line formats are DPL/FairMQ and DataDistribution, TfBuilderTask); briefs/constraints.md:87-91 (DDS is a separate family)
fix: Write "Later rounds added the second process-tree format, written by the data-distribution processes, plus the InfoLogger daemon log and the system journal." and name both formats once in Section 2.1.

problem: The sentence has no object, and the reader took it to mean the bus is separate from the four reopen conditions rather than a separate decision.
source: briefs/soak-index.md:9 ("Two Kafka decisions exist and stay apart")
fix: Write "The live-lane bus of Section 4 is a separate decision."
